synopsis: Unity is identified as one of the two best-known game engines and is used in both a 2026 off-road digital-twin simulator and the TERA autonomous-excavator simulator [f13171, f13175, f3790, f4129]. The digital twin includes procedural terrain, multiple cameras, lidar, GPS, IMU, dynamic weather and lighting, and failure annotations; TERA combines Unity with AGX, configurable excavators and environments, ROS integration, and terrain-machine interaction [f3790, f4129]. The tool survey lists supported AGX integration with Unity, a Unity lidar module, and Project Chrono Unity interfaces; the glossary dates an AGX Unity reverse auto-brake example with lidar to April 2025 [f8703, f9108, f9025, f15967]. Procedural datasets and ready-made Unity assets support virtual job-site creation, but a 2026 study found Unity-rendered construction scenes still diverged from real photometric distributions despite extensive domain randomization; that study is identified as a preprint [f3733, f3832, f10584, f10585].
